issues.description: The problem statement instructs students to mark the end of the main loop with the label `loop_end`, but the template file does not include any `loop_end` label and the solution uses a different label name `end_loop`. This mismatch between the specified label name and the solution/template can confuse students about the exact label they must add and causes an inconsistency between the problem description and the provided solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the label name consistent across all artifacts. Either change the solution label `end_loop` to `loop_end` and add `loop_end:` in the template at the intended location (before `ret`), or update the problem statement to request `end_loop` instead of `loop_end`. Ensure the template includes the requested label so students can follow the instruction.

issues.description: The problem statement instructs students to mark the end of the main loop with the label `loop_end` (problem_statement.md line 22), but the solution uses the label `end_loop` in helloWorld.asm. The template does not provide the `loop_end` label either. This inconsistent label naming across artifacts can confuse students who look for `loop_end` in the provided code or in the solution, increasing extraneous cognitive load when mapping the requirement to the implementation.
issues.suggestedFix: Use a single consistent label name across all artifacts. Rename the solution label `end_loop:` to `loop_end:` (and add `loop_end:` to the template at the end of the main loop if intended), or update the problem statement to require `end_loop` instead. Prefer changing the solution/template to `loop_end` to match the problem text.
